extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Indian agents, Commissioners of Indian Affairs, treaty negotiators, and Congressional policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Text of late-19th-century agreements and accompanying annual-report tables specifying conditions for cession, allotment, patenting, appropriations, and statistical metrics for Indian reservations; also contract quality specifications for supplies to the Indian service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey and issuance of patents for allotted lands
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government of the United States shall cause the agricultural lands remaining in the reservation to be properly surveyed and divided among the Indians in severalty, and shall issue patents to them respectively therefor so soon as the necessary laws are passed by Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys and division are a precondition to issuing patents; issuance is to follow enactment of enabling laws by Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allotments in severalty — sizes and grazing allowancess
rubrics_metrics.description: Allotments in severalty of said surveyed lands shall be made as follows: To each head of a family not more than one-quarter of a section, with an additional quantity of grazing-land not exceeding one-quarter of a section. To each single person over eighteen years of age not more than one-eighth of a section, with an additional quantity of grazing-land not exceeding one-eighth of a section. To each orphan child under eighteen years of age not more than one-eighth of a section, with an additional quantity of grazing-land not exceeding one-eighth of a section; and to each other person, under eighteen years, or who may be born prior to said allotments, one-eighth of a section, with a like quantity of grazing-land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives precise fractional-section allotment caps (1/4 or 1/8) and matches grazing-land allowances to the residential allotment fraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allotment selection and administrative advice
rubrics_metrics.description: All allotments to be made with the advice of the agent for said Indians, or such other person as the Secretary of the Interior may designate for that purpose, upon the selection of the Indians, heads of families selecting for their minor children, and the agent making the allotment for each orphan child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection process: Indians choose allotments; heads choose for minors; agent makes allotments for orphan children; the agent or Secretary's designee provides advice and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title restrictions — inalienability and tax exemption period
rubrics_metrics.description: The title to be acquired by the Indians shall not be subject to alienation, lease, or incumbrance, either by voluntary conveyance of the grantee or his heirs, or by the judgment, order, or decree of any court, or subject to taxation of any character, but shall be and remain inalienable, and not subject to taxation for the period of twenty-five years, and until such time thereafter as the President may see fit to remove the restriction, which shall be incorporated in the patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction period is 25 years (minimum) and continues until the President acts; restriction language must be incorporated into the issued patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation for transition assistance (Crow agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: In consideration of the cession the United States agrees to appropriate annually for twenty-five years the sum of thirty thousand dollars, to be expended under the direction of the President for the benefit of said Indians, in assisting them to erect houses, to procure seeds, farming implements, stock, or in cash, as the President may direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds are dedicated to settlement/agricultural transition expenses and are subject to Presidential direction; duration 25 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grazing access fees and disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If at any time hereafter the Crow Indians shall consent to permit cattle to be driven across their reservation or grazed on the same, the Secretary of the Interior shall fix the amount to be paid by parties desiring so to drive or graze cattle; all moneys arising from this source to be paid to the Indians under such rules and regulations as the Secretary of the Interior may prescribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary of the Interior sets fees; receipts are payable to Indians and distributed under Secretary-prescribed rules/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of prior treaty provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: All existing provisions of the treaty of May seventh, 1868, shall continue in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New agreement articles are supplemental; prior treaty terms remain effective unless expressly changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annuity payments for Lemhi and Fort Hall cessions
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States agree to pay to the Lemhi Indians the sum of four thousand dollars per annum for twenty years, and to the Fort Hall Indians the sum of six thousand dollars per annum for twenty years, the same to be in addition to any sums to which the above-named Indians are now entitled by treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments are additive to existing treaty payments; term specified is twenty years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey, division, and patent issuance for Fort Hall (and related) reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government of the United States shall cause the lands of the Fort Hall Reservation to be properly surveyed and to be divided among the said Indians in severalty in the proportions hereinbefore mentioned, and shall issue patents to them respectively therefor so soon as the necessary laws are passed by Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same mechanism as other agreements — surveys and patenting contingent on congressional action; ensures allotments in severalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of inalienability and tax restriction in patents (Fort Hall/Shoshone)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title to be acquired thereto by the Indians shall not be subject to alienation, lease, or incumbrance ... but shall be and remain inalienable and not subject to taxation for the period of twenty-five years, and until such time thereafter as the President may see fit to remove the restriction, which shall be incorporated in the patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors the Crow agreement restriction; requirement to place restriction clause explicitly in issued patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical metrics reported (recapitulation of agricultural statistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report tabulates: Number of acres in Indian reservations; Number of acres tillable; Number of whites unlawfully on reserves; Number of acres occupied by white intruders; Number of acres cultivated by the government during the year; Number of acres cultivated by school children during the year; Number of acres cultivated by Indians during the year; Number of acres broken by the government during the year; Number of acres broken by Indians during the year; Number of allotments made in severalty to Indians; Number of rods of fencing made during the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items form the core agricultural/statistical fields used in the annual report; they are counted and recapitulated across agencies and used to summarize produce, stock, and other results of Indian labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural production and livestock metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report further enumerates bushels of wheat, corn, oats and barley, vegetables, tons of hay, melons, pumpkins; stock counts including horses, mules, cattle, swine, sheep; other results such as cords of wood cut, feet of lumber sawed, value of robes and furs sold, pounds of wool raised, number of shingles made, number of barrel staves made, pounds of maple-sugar, willow baskets, barrels of fish sold, cords of hemlock bark pared for sale, bushels of berries, bushels of wild rice, pounds of butter, gallons of maple sirup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These production and output categories are the reported outcome metrics used to evaluate agricultural/subsistence activity on reservations and government/school/Indian contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement quality specification — Bacon
rubrics_metrics.description: Bacon — To be 'short, clear sides,' winter cured, sound, and put up in gunnies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality and packing specification for bacon supply contracts to the Indian service; 'gunnies' refers to gunny sacks (burlap) for delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement quality specification — Barley
rubrics_metrics.description: Barley — Sound and clean, and put up in barrels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract quality/packing requirement for barley deliveries; pricing/rates appear elsewhere in tabulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement quality specification — Beans
rubrics_metrics.description: Beans — To be of good merchantable quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General merchantable-quality standard; specific grading not provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement quality specification — Corn
rubrics_metrics.description: Corn — Full whole grain, sound, sweet and clean, weighing not less than 56 pounds to the bushel; to be delivered in well-sewed gunnies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies weight-per-bushel minimum, condition (sound/sweet/clean), and packaging (well-sewed gunny sacks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement quality specification — Flour
rubrics_metrics.description: Flour — 'Straight, full stock' of good, sound wheat (60 pounds of wheat to the bushel indicated in adjacent tabulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification phrasing 'straight, full stock' indicates an unadulterated, full-weight product of sound wheat; detailed milling/grading standards not fully transcribed on this page.
